messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: high KV-cache memory growth detected on cluster-prod-us-east-1. Affected service: runtime-tp-kv. Autoresponder created incident ID #INC-2026-0421. Metrics: kv_cache_total_bytes +400% in 5m, NCCL stall rate spike.

maya: i'm on it — paging eng-runtime and oncall backup. adding context: continuous-batching rollout from last night to 1.2.7.

raj: seeing repeated NCCL WARNs in pod runtime-tp-.*: 
```
W NCCL: NCCL comm ring stalled: op allreduce, peer rank mismatch, timeout
E runtime: kv_shard imbalance detected: shard_weights = [0.02, 0.48, 0.49, 0.01]
```
This looks like uneven KV shard partitioning interacting badly with continuous batching leading to blowup.

sasha: confirm metrics — batch token size distribution shifted right after rollout, avg_batch_tokens went from 512 -> 2300 for top 20% flows. prefix caching + big batches = memory blowout.

maya: customer impact? claire-cs?

claire-cs: getting reports from 2 enterprise customers, timeouts and elevated latencies 5xxs on chat endpoints. CS pinged them and opened support tickets. No data exfil reported.

ava: handoff to me for mitigation loop. initial plan: 1) disable continuous-batching on affected pools 2) reduce max_batch_tokens to 768 3) rebalance KV shard mapping and respawn TP pods 4) monitor NCCL error rate and cache size.

maya: +1. can we toggle batch flags via runtime feature flags without deploy?

raj: yes, we have feature flags. Commands: 
```
# disable continuous batching for pool prod-kv-tp
rictl feature-set --pool prod-kv-tp --feature continuous_batching=false
# reduce max batch tokens
rictl config-set --pool prod-kv-tp --key max_batch_tokens --value 768
```
I'll apply in 60s unless objections.

tom: recommend also issuing per-shard KV cache cap to avoid one-hot blowups: 
```
rictl kv-config --shard tp-2 --set max_entries=1e6
rictl kv-config --shard tp-3 --set max_entries=1e6
```

ava: applying flags now. i'll post outputs.

ava: (applied) continuous_batching=false -> success. max_batch_tokens -> 768. per-shard caps set for tp-2,tp-3.

raj: seeing immediate drop in avg_batch_tokens tail. NCCL stalls still spiking but error rate falling. cache_total_bytes growth rate slowed from +400% -> +40% in next 3m.

sasha: adding quick mitigation: evict top-k entries from shards with disproportionate weight to get memory headroom: 
```
rictl kv-evict --shard tp-3 --policy top_entries --count 20000
```

ava: eviction started. will watch for 10m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT #INC-2026-0421 update: mitigation flags applied. Status: partial_mitigation. Escalation: eng-runtime oncall engaged.

claire-cs: letting customers know we applied mitigations and latency should improve within ~15min. thanks.

maya: are we sure this is just config + shard imbalance and not a code-level regression in the TP kv shard assignment?

raj: logs show shard assignment function produced skewed weights after the continuous-batching change — sampling logic used sequence-length distribution which shifted under new batching assumptions. probable cause: code didn't account for batched KV prefix accumulation across tensor-parallel ranks -> some shards saw disproportionate prefix reuse, leading to hot partitions. I want a hotfix to shard mapper to use modulo-based fallback when weights exceed 0.3 variance. I'll open a hotpatch.

sasha: while you draft hotfix, we should keep continuous_batching off in prod pools. also add alert to detect shard_weight variance > 0.25.

raj: hotpatch commit ready, small change in shard_mapper.c: if variance > 0.25 -> fallback_to_round_robin = true. I'll push and rollout to one region canary.

raj: rolling patch to canary group now: kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-tp-canary.

maya: handoff note: ava remains on watch for 1hr, i'll stay available. once canary clears in 10m, roll to prod. please post metrics for NCCL errors, kv cache bytes, p99 latency.

ava: canary looks good after 8m. NCCL stalls dropped to baseline, cache growth plateaued. rolling to prod in 2 batches.

incident-bot: INCIDENT #INC-2026-0421 update: hotpatch applied to prod (batch A). Monitoring.

ava: prod batch A rolled, metrics positive. rolling batch B.

raj: batch B done. no regressions observed. added automated guard: if kv_cache_growth_rate > 50% over 5m -> auto-disable continuous_batching and notify.

sasha: re-enabled controlled continuous-batching in canary with updated shard mapper to validate behavior under normal load. so far stable. we'll keep continuous_batching disabled on prod pools for now until we validate with long tail tests.

claire-cs: customers informed: reduced impact; follow-ups scheduled.

maya: postmortem owners: raj (root cause / code fix), sasha (workload + batching config), ava (mitigation runbook updates), claire-cs (customer comms). Please capture timeline and retrospective.

ava: writing runbook patch now: add step to cap per-shard entries, eviction command example, and emergency flag toggles. Also adding link to debug dashboard panels for shard_weights, NCCL errors, avg_batch_tokens tail.

tom: added a small script to automate shard rebalancing if variance > threshold: 
```
# quick rebalance
python tools/rebalance_kv_shards.py --cluster prod --threshold 0.25 --dry-run
```

incident-bot: INCIDENT #INC-2026-0421 resolved -> mitigations stable and hotfix deployed. Close reason: config + mapper hotfix mitigated blowup and eliminated NCCL stalls.

maya: thanks everyone. please file the postmortem doc and link to incident thread. :thumbsup:

claire-cs: closing customer tickets as workaround verified. will follow up if anything else.

ava: final notes: suspected contributing factors: 1) continuous-batching increased correlated prefix reuse 2) shard mapper sensitivity to distribution shifts 3) missing per-shard caps. Action items: enforce per-shard caps by default, add variance alert, QA continuous-batching behavior in staging with synthetic long-tail traces.

sasha: I'll generate replay traces and perf cliffs report.

maya: closing thread. thanks all.
